description: This Python generator creates planning inputs for reconfigurable radio-access and optical X-haul networks. Brianna Laird publishes a workflow that extracts road topology and generates candidate radio, distributed-unit and central-unit locations, demand clusters, hotspots and connectivity paths. Users provide a geographic polygon and parameters for device capacity, coverage, ports, user distributions and backup locations. Outputs include generated dataset files, maps and JSON configuration summaries. Coverage is user-selected geographic regions and static planning scenarios; no fixed observation period or traffic sampling interval is established. The source code is freely available under GPL 3.0. The inspected tree contains generation scripts but no populated dataset directory, so this record covers the tool, not a released collection of region-specific data. A limitation is that central-unit positions, road edges and generated paths may require manual correction. Upstream map rights remain separate from the software licence. Simulation uses include creating capacity-planning and optimisation cases for the linked B5G planning algorithms. It relates to data-openstreetmap as a possible road-network source, with source details to confirm for each generated case. No generator was executed.
name: B5G network planning dataset generator
